questions.q: What does `incremental_strategy` control, as distinct from `is_incremental()`?
options: What dbt does with the selected rows once found (merge, delete+insert, append), while is_incremental() decides which rows get selected
Whether the model is materialized as a view or a table
The warehouse the model connects to
Whether tests run before or after the model builds
questions.explain: is_incremental() gates which rows the SELECT returns on a repeat run; incremental_strategy controls how those rows get applied to the target table.

questions.q: Which strategy compiles to a real MERGE statement, matching on unique_key?
options: merge
append
delete+insert
None of them use MERGE
questions.explain: merge is the default strategy and compiles to a MERGE statement — the same shape already familiar from T-SQL and Snowflake.

questions.q: When is `delete+insert` the better choice over `merge`?
options: When a whole batch naturally replaces a whole prior batch, or on a warehouse where MERGE is unsupported or slow
Only when the model has zero rows
Never — merge is always strictly better in every case
Only for seeds, never for models
questions.explain: delete+insert deletes rows matching the new batch's keys and inserts the batch wholesale — a better fit when replacing whole batches, or where MERGE isn't well supported.

options: Because it does no matching at all — it just inserts the new rows, which is only safe for truly immutable, append-only data
Because append automatically deduplicates rows for you
Because unique_key is required for every strategy except append, by design flaw
Because append only works on seeds
questions.explain: append is the cheapest strategy because it skips matching entirely — that's exactly why it's unsafe for data that can be updated after it first arrives.

questions.q: What happens if you use `append` on data that can be updated after arrival?
options: You get duplicate rows the moment a changed row looks like a 'new' row to the filter
dbt automatically falls back to merge behavior
The model fails to compile
Nothing — append behaves identically to merge in every case
questions.explain: Without matching, append can't tell a changed row from a brand-new one — if the filter picks it up again, it gets inserted a second time as a duplicate.
